minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard fire, special ed and facilities budgets; a member said the override has no chance of passing.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the fire chief's FY25 budget presentation, then questioned the school special services director and the new facilities director ahead of the full school presentation. Discussion covered circuit breaker, bargaining, school cuts, building repairs, snow removal and ARPA offsets. The committee also went over draft warrant articles and Chapter 90 funds. The only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none was offered.
Urged succession planning for facilities, consolidating town and school facilities, starting budget talks with department heads in August, and questioned a school plow truck and school-run benefits.
Follow-up question on what the school truck is used for outside plowing; school staff answered.

budget_items.what_was_said: Bids came in under the office estimate and the contract was awarded to PJ Keating.
The new growth certificate was approved and the additional new growth will be added to the school budget; overlay stays unchanged.
Level service budget with contractual salary increases and full paramedic coverage.
Above-target request for EMS supplies is in the town manager's proposed budget.
Requested increase for radio maintenance has not been funded; the line has not risen in 10 to 15 years.
Doing paramedic service in-house saved on outside ALS payments.
Reimbursement is forecast at various rates; recent years were reimbursed at the high end.
Prior year tuition rate rose sharply, absorbed by carryover; the Keystone collaborative is looking at a large increase.
A contractual stipend line is new in the local budget, previously paid from a revolving account.
A member estimated first-year contract cost across the three budgets.
Elevator repair and failed inspection led to a second quote.
Controller replacement is in next year's budget; technician and rooftop repair costs were described.
A line was included for work to move the Ace Program to Turkey Hill.
A member noted the contracted services line seems low for four buildings.
Skipping the annual deposit would be viewed poorly by bond rating; amount is a share of prior free cash.

budget_items.topic: Classification study impact and salary reserve
budget_items.what_was_said: The impact comes first out of the salary reserve account.
An article may be paid from ARPA; balance mentioned.
About the stated amount sits in Chapter 90; sidewalk work may be shifted from ARPA.
Parks was awarded a grant bringing secured grant money up.
Water district treatment plant and sewer rate increases were noted.

decisions.decision: School staff will answer committee questions within days; IT phone-system cost information is due by end of day Tuesday.
Revenue and expenditure recap discussion deferred until August.
Minutes will be put up for approval at the next meeting.
Chair will ask whether the finance committee report for the warrant can be due a few days after the first April meeting.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the fire chief's FY25 budget presentation, described as a level-service budget with contractual raises and full paramedic coverage.
Members questioned school special education staff on circuit breaker reimbursement, out-of-district tuition increases and bargaining costs.
The new facilities director took questions on elevator repair, the building controller, HVAC and snow removal.
The committee deferred the revenue and expenditure recap discussion until August; school staff owe answers within days, with IT phone-system costs due Tuesday.
No votes on budget items were taken; the only vote was adjournment.

why_it_matters: The school and fire figures heard here are FY25 requests still under review, so the tax bill effect is not yet set, and out-of-district tuition and circuit breaker reimbursement are the lines that can move the school's share most.
Part of the school's FY25 budget now rests on a contractual stipend line that was previously paid from a revolving account, which moves a cost onto the tax-funded budget.
watch_next: School staff answers to committee questions, including IT phone-system cost information due by end of day Tuesday.
The chair's question on whether the finance committee report for the warrant can be due a few days after the first April meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree that there were no non-procedural votes, and they agree on most headline figures (2.21% fire budget, $127,000/$634,000 road bid, 11%/14% tuition rates, $25,000 stipends, $14,800 elevator, 1.9 million Chapter 90, Parks grant). Our minutes carry many more figures and several decisions the official minutes omit, and the one amount a person should check is radio maintenance: $110,000 in ours versus a $10,000 increase in the official minutes.
